evidence.note: Unscoped `Project.find(params[:id])` lets any user access any project; scope it: `@current_user.projects.find(params[:id])`.
API1:2023, the #1 API risk: validate that the logged-in user may access the record the request id names.
Maintainer blog: LLM judges detect missing authorization best when the check is self-contained in the function or absent entirely -- the snippet-visible case this rule targets.

rb-unscoped-find.whyNotLinter: RuboCop/rubocop-rails have no authorization cop. Brakeman's UnscopedFind check is optional (not in the default run) and name-based; it cannot see Pundit/CanCan calls or public-by-nature models.
rb-unscoped-find.aiRelevance: High: scaffold-style controllers generated by agents use `Model.find(params[:id])`; CodeRabbit (C) reports more security issues in AI PRs.
rb-unscoped-find.expectedNoise: med -- authorization may be in a `before_action` or concern outside the snippet; dry-run before enabling by default.

evidence.note: Sanitize or allow-list user-provided column names for `order`.

rb-sql-interpolation.whyNotLinter: RuboCop has no SQL-injection cop. Brakeman catches most interpolation cases if it gates CI -- disable this rule (config `disable`) in those repos; it stays useful for the many repos without Brakeman in CI.
rb-sql-interpolation.aiRelevance: Medium: agents write `order("#{params[:sort]} #{params[:dir]}")` for sortable tables.
rb-sql-interpolation.expectedNoise: low -- allow-listed interpolation is named in `false`.

evidence.note: Rails 8.1 guide: 'If you're unsure whether your code relies on transactional integrity, enabling enqueue_after_transaction_commit globally in ApplicationJob is the safest default' -- i.e. it is not implicit.
Jobs execute 'at least once'; enqueue with simple identifiers that must exist when the job runs.

rb-side-effect-before-commit.whyNotLinter: Rails/AfterCommitOverride and ActiveRecordCallbacksOrder only check callback declarations; nothing recognises external side effects inside transactions or save callbacks. Sidekiq's `perform_async` ignores Rails' enqueue-after-commit setting.
rb-side-effect-before-commit.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): agents add `after_create :send_welcome_email` and `perform_async` inside `transaction do` blocks.
rb-side-effect-before-commit.expectedNoise: low -- both the transaction/callback and the side effect must be visible.

evidence.note: Mass assignment: 'every parameter may be changed'; permit explicitly, never `permit!`.

rb-privileged-attrs-permitted.whyNotLinter: RuboCop has no cop for which attributes are privileged. Brakeman warns on `permit!` and a fixed list of dangerous keys when it runs, but cannot tell admin controllers or policy-gated permits from user-facing ones.
rb-privileged-attrs-permitted.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): agents copy every model column into `permit(...)`, including `role`/`user_id`.
rb-privileged-attrs-permitted.expectedNoise: low-med -- admin/policy context is usually visible in the same controller.

evidence.note: 'In Ruby ^ and $ match the line beginning and line end'; use \A and \z; example bypass with an embedded newline.

rb-line-anchor-validation-regex.whyNotLinter: Rails raises for `validates format:` with `^`/`$` unless `multiline: true`, and Brakeman's ValidationRegex covers model validations only. `=~`/`match?` guards in controllers and services are not checked, and whether a regex validates vs parses needs judgment.
rb-line-anchor-validation-regex.aiRelevance: Medium: `^...$` is the idiom models learn from JavaScript; in Ruby it is a bypass.
rb-line-anchor-validation-regex.expectedNoise: low -- parsing multi-line text is excluded.

evidence.note: Optimistic (`lock_version`) and pessimistic (`lock`, `with_lock`) locking for concurrent updates.

rb-read-modify-write-race.whyNotLinter: Needs to recognise shared numeric state and the absence of a lock. Note Rails/SkipsModelValidations flags the atomic fixes (`update_counters`, `update_all`); repos may need a disable comment there.
rb-read-modify-write-race.aiRelevance: Medium-high (inferred): agents implement credits/inventory as plain attribute arithmetic.

evidence.note: rubocop-rails added Rails/FindByOrAssignmentMemoization for the `@x ||= find_by` case, showing maintainers treat it as a recurring bug; it covers only find_by.
Existing menu candidate in this repo (unvalidated).

rb-memoize-nil-or-false.whyNotLinter: Rails/FindByOrAssignmentMemoization covers only `find_by`; predicates, ENV, API calls and `detect` need judgment about nil-ability.
rb-memoize-nil-or-false.aiRelevance: Medium: agents apply `||=` memoization to everything.

rb-rescue-swallowed.whyNotLinter: Lint/SuppressedException defaults to AllowComments: true and AllowNil: true, and Style/RescueModifier only flags syntax; returning a default silently is not checked.
rb-rescue-swallowed.aiRelevance: High: agents add `rescue => e; nil` / `rescue StandardError; {}` to make errors go away.
